newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK property stocks take beating after govt move.
newsitem.headline: HK property stocks take beating after govt move.

text.p: Hong Kong's property stocks took a beating on Thursday following the government's move on Wednesday to curb escalating property prices by bringing more supply to the market.
The Hong Kong government said it would extend the presale period for private flats to 15 months from a current 12 months.
"It will give less possibility for developers to price their products," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at PrimeEast Securities.
Shares in Henderson Land fell HK$1.75 to HK$65.00, Sun Hung Kai Properties dropped HK$1.50 to HK$83.75.
Cheung Kong fell HK$1.25 to HK$69.25 and New World Development slumped HK$1.60 to HK$41.90.

Eric Yuen, property analyst at Daiwa Institute of Research, said companies like Henderson Land would be "seriously affected" because they tend to release flats for sale in small batches, increasing the price for each new batch.
He expected prices in the mass residential market to correct some 10 percent after their sharp run, hit by the measure and higher interest rates.
"The (property) stocks are likely to consolidate. I don't think they will continue to underperform but it is very unlikely for them to outperform over the next three months," he said.
